To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose a novel framework for privacy preserving re-publications of dynamic datasets, and 2) we provide the first privacy preserving data re-publication solution, that supports both insertions and deletions, and 3) we show that our framework and solution are efficient and scalable.
we have developed a novel framework, which is the first to support re-publication of microdata with insertions and deletions.
the proposed approach is: (1) efficient (in terms of the time required to re-publish the data) and (2) secure, as the re-published data does not contain any information about the original data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: given a dataset that has been updated with both insertions and deletions, how can the publisher provide the researchers with the most current data without revealing any sensitive information?
the problem of publishing a dataset that is continuously updated with insertions and deletions, in such a way that a user is unable to identify any of its elements.

the following problem: <u>How can a publisher re-publish a dynamic dataset while preserving the privacy of the individuals in the database?</u> To address the above problem, we introduce the concept of <u>M-invariance</u>.

the current state-of-the-art does not provide a solution for re-publishing microdata that has been updated with both insertions and deletions.
there is currently no solution that supports privacy preserving re-publications of dynamic microdata.
the current literature does not provide solutions to the re-publication problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed an efficient solution for re-publication of datasets with insertions and deletions.
we provide an efficient and secure way to update a dataset with insertions and deletions.

we have proposed a new privacy model for data publication, called M-invariance, that allows for re-publication of data with insertions and deletions, and that is based on a new notion of differential privacy, called microaggregation differential privacy, that is more realistic than the existing one.

, if we want to support the dynamic nature of microdata publication, we need to change the way privacy is defined and measured.
